title: Line complications during outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy: an explanatory sequential mixed methods study of patients, lines and home care
abstract: Objective: to estimate line complication rates during outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy and explain their variation. Design: explanatory sequential mixed methods; a linked record cohort of OPAT episodes from 2021 to 2025, then interviews with patients, carers and agency nurses sampled from the cohort's extremes. Primary outcome: line complication with unplanned hospital contact or premature removal per 1,000 catheter days. Results and conclusions will be written after both strands.
introduction: Line complications are the main reason for unplanned returns during home intravenous antibiotic therapy. Retrieved studies show rates vary between nursing teams and that hospital records miss problems managed at home, but no local data exist.
methods: Records of about 1,870 episodes are linked and complications coded with a written definition; Poisson regression with a catheter-day offset estimates rates by line type and care arrangement. About 28 interviews sampled from high- and low-complication groups are analysed with the framework method, and a joint display integrates the strands.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the cohort flow, complication rates by exposure, the proportion of complications found only in agency notes if shared, interview themes, and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will set the local rates beside the retrieved studies, explain agency and patient differences with the interview findings, and state where the service should act first.
limitations: Complications managed at home may be missed if the agency notes are not shared; confounding by line choice; one service.
conclusion: To be written after integration; it will not claim that any change reduces complications, which would need a separate evaluation.
reportingChecklist: GRAMMS for the mixed methods report, with STROBE for strand 1 and COREQ for strand 2
summary: GRAMMS-structured draft with results left empty until both strands are complete.
